test.title: Bench Test Results: Amprius INR21700/50Q (no CCC) - 50A 5000mAh 21700 - Is it 5000Q?
test.author: Mooch

temperature_points.context: Never exceed the battery’s true continuous discharge rating (CDR), never let it get colder than 0°C or hotter than 60°C to help lower the risks and extend cell life, and keep the plastic wrap and top insulating ring in perfect condition.
The cells I had reached over their 80°C limit at 50A down to 2.5V by a few degrees-C so I’m rating them at 40A true continuous.
The datasheet lists a 125A “max discharge current” rating, temperature-limited to 75°C.
But there was already a lot of voltage sag at 100A so I am giving it a temp-limited (to 75°C) rating of 100A.
Cycle life is listed as >=300 cycles at +5A/-50A to 2.50V or 75°C for a drop to 70% of original capacity.

temperature_points.context: Never exceed the battery’s true continuous discharge rating (CDR), never let it get colder than 0°C or hotter than 60°C to help lower the risks and extend cell life, and keep the plastic wrap and top insulating ring in perfect condition.
Datasheet “max continuous discharge current” spec is 40A and 60A when temp-limited to 75°C.
Tenpower says you can run this cell at up to 60A but to never let it go over 75°C.
For discharges at 40A and lower the max cell temp is 80°C.
Stopping at 75°C helps reduce risk and accelerated cell aging (reduced cycle life).
The 60XG PP samples I tested went a bit over 80°C at 40A down to 2.5V so I’ll be rating these samples at 35A true continuous (80°C max limit) and 60A temp-limited (to 75°C).
It lasts at least 200 or 300 cycles at +6A/-40A (75°C cutoff) down to 2.5V before dropping to 70% of the original capacity.
